properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-31. Nothing chosen. His words: "maybe we defined 10 subsystems independent of what the structure actually is and we can't seem to reconcile them. maybe the better approach is to forget the 10 subsystems and define new boundaries based on the actual structure of the code? then we can at least get to some defined black-boxes that agree with the structure of the actual code?"

📌 CREATED VIA create_node after searching and reading the near-matches in full; relations drawn with review_relations (add_decision's `related_to` route does not serialise from this client).

═══ WHAT THE RECORD ALREADY ANSWERS, so this starts from the frontier ═══
· The ten WERE defined independent of code structure, deliberately — `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`, accepted 2026-07-23, derived with him. Structure-derived was not an unconsidered option; it was the state being escaped: the self-model had been recovered backwards from the file tree and the domain primitives a design-graph tool IS appeared nowhere.
· The code-derived spine was offered AGAIN on 2026-08-25 with the artefact in hand — adopt had recovered the module hierarchy, top tier `cmp:crate-reflow2-core` / `cmp:crate-reflow2-mcp` — and was declined on the record.
· The 10-vs-actual mismatch is REAL but is in the PROSE: 8 of the ten sit at `level: subsystem` and two at `level: system` with five children each. The spine itself is clean — hierarchy_issues 0, multiple_parents 0. See `fact:the-ten-subsystems-are-eighteen-and-the-decision-that-names-them-was-never-amended`.

═══ 🛑 THE NEW ARGUMENT, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE STATED GOAL ═══
The goal is "black boxes that agree with the structure of the actual code". Measured 2026-08-31: 88 core modules, 45 of them adding methods to the SHARED `DesignGraph` struct across 62 impl blocks, graph.rs alone carrying 54; and 56 of 64 uncovered coupling pairs have `impl DesignGraph` on BOTH ends, crossing no crate boundary.

⇒ THE CODE HAS NO BLACK-BOX BOUNDARIES TO AGREE WITH. Re-deriving the spine from structure would produce two crates and a module list — which is what adopt produced, and what was declined twice. It would not produce black boxes, because a black box needs encapsulated STATE and 45 modules share one struct's. **A carving cannot discover a boundary the code does not have.**

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
① KEEP THE FUNCTIONAL SPINE, AMEND ITS PROSE. Cheapest and honest: the structure is coherent, only its describing decision is stale. Buys nothing new.
② RE-DERIVE FROM THE MODULES, as proposed. Would reproduce the crate/module view declined twice, and by today's measurement would not yield black boxes.
③ RE-DERIVE FROM CO-CHANGE — the one branch with data. Measured 2026-08-21: 536 co-change observations between Components, 380 of them (71%) CROSSING a current subsystem boundary, and the signal survives removing `cmp:service` as a confound (70%). Leiden on that graph would run today and would produce a MATERIALLY different decomposition. It answers "what changes together", i.e. maintainability.
④ PICK THE ILITY FIRST, THEN THE GRAPH — his own 2026-08-08 idea. Note it has ALREADY been done once: the coherence-loop split was made by the OBSERVABILITY cut, and that decision says so in as many words ("the quality target was not decoration; it picked the cut").
⑤ SPLIT THE STRUCT. The only option that actually creates black boxes, and it is a code change rather than a carving. Large, and nothing has yet been blocked by the current shape.

⚠️ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside rather than used to argue the idea down. (1) 71% disagreement measures DIFFERENCE, not improvement — nothing compares the two decompositions against any outcome anybody cares about. (2) The performance branch is not even runnable: `evaluate_allocation` reports ONE capability-to-capability dependency edge in the whole design, so Leiden on the dependency graph has nothing to cluster. (3) This project has twice retired metric-driven verdicts that fired on correct architecture, so a purely computed allocator has a recorded failure mode here. (4) A service boundary carries obligations no coupling graph encodes — deployment unit, failure domain, ownership, release cadence.

⭐ THE QUESTION UNDERNEATH ALL FIVE, and it may be the one worth answering first: WHAT IS THE SPINE FOR? If it is for explaining the product to a reader, function wins and the code view stays evidence. If it is for bounding change, co-change wins. If it is for substitution or independent optimisation, none of them wins until the struct is split.
properties.name: OPEN — should the functional spine be abandoned for boundaries derived from actual structure, and if so from WHICH structure: the modules, the co-change graph, or an ility?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm discipline — ideas as ideas, nothing promoted, and the two prior declines recorded beside the proposal rather than used to close it. He has now raised structure-derived allocation three times (2026-08-08 as graph-theoretic clustering, 2026-08-21 as "draw a boundary around the communities", 2026-08-31 as "forget the ten"), and each time the answer has turned on WHICH GRAPH rather than on yes or no. That the question keeps returning in different words is itself evidence the prior answers never reached him — the same pattern as the four stale records found this session.
